title: [PDF] Final rule to modify the enhanced supplementary leverage ratio standards
summary: The Federal Reserve, FDIC, and OCC issued a final rule on November 5, 2025, modifying enhanced supplementary leverage ratio (eSLR) standards for U.S. GSIBs and their subsidiary depository institutions. The rule reduces eSLR buffers to half of the method 1 GSIB surcharge (capped at 1% for subsidiaries) to ensure leverage ratios function as a backstop rather than a binding constraint, with the stated goal of supporting Treasury market functioning.
key_points: Final rule modifies eSLR buffer standard for GSIBs to equal 50% of the method 1 surcharge under the Board's GSIB surcharge framework
Subsidiary depository institutions of GSIBs receive a buffer equal to half of parent GSIB's method 1 surcharge, capped at 1%
Conforming changes made to total loss-absorbing capacity (TLAC) and long-term debt requirements
Effective date is April 1, 2026, with early adoption permitted beginning January 1, 2026
Rule aims to reduce regulatory disincentives for GSIBs to engage in market intermediation, particularly in U.S. Treasury markets
Currently, supplementary leverage ratio requirements have become binding constraints rather than backstops, creating perverse incentives according to the agencies
why_it_matters: This regulatory change affects capital requirements for the largest U.S. banks (GSIBs), potentially reducing their leverage capital buffers. By reducing the likelihood that eSLR is binding, the agencies hope to encourage GSIB-affiliated broker-dealers to continue intermediating in Treasury markets, which is critical for market liquidity and price discovery.
market_structure_context: The rule directly addresses Treasury market structure by modifying capital requirements that affect GSIB market-making capacity. When eSLR is binding, it creates disincentives for broker-dealers to intermediate in Treasury markets because leverage requirements apply equally to low-risk assets like Treasuries. The agencies explicitly note this can create problems for smooth functioning of the U.S. Treasury market.
important_numbers: 50% of method 1 surcharge (eSLR buffer for GSIBs)
1% cap (maximum eSLR buffer for subsidiary depository institutions)
